Phylogenetic community structure against the dynamic null model of DAMOCLES

Source: R/damocles.R
damocles_test.Rd

damocles_test() compares the mean pairwise distance (MPD) and the mean nearest taxon distance (MNTD) among the species present in each community with two null distributions: one from communities simulated along the tree under the DAMOCLES model (Pigot & Etienne 2015; simulate_damocles()), with the rates of colonisation and local extinction estimated from that community (or shared by all communities) by damocles_fit() or given, and one from random draws of the same number of species from the tips, the static null model the dynamic one is compared with in that study.

Usage

damocles_test(
  comm,
  tree,
  n_sim = 999,
  gamma = NULL,
  mu = NULL,
  root = c("both", "absent", "present"),
  shared = FALSE,
  sympatry = 0,
  regimes = NULL,
  edge_covariate = NULL,
  vary = c("both", "gamma", "mu")
)

Arguments

comm

Presences of the species (columns, named as the tips of tree) in one or more communities (rows): a matrix or data frame, or a named vector for one community. Values above zero count as presences. Tips missing from comm count as absent, with a warning, and species of comm missing from the tree are dropped.

tree

A rooted, fully dichotomous phylo tree with branch lengths.

n_sim

Number of null communities of each model.

gamma, mu

Rates of local colonisation and extinction used to simulate the null communities, one value for all communities or one per community, or lists with one rate, or one rate per edge of tree, per community; NULL (the default) estimates both with damocles_fit(), with shared, sympatry, regimes, edge_covariate and vary passed on to it.

root

Prior on the state at the root, used both in the fit and in the simulations ("both" draws the state of the root of each simulated community with equal probabilities).

shared

When the rates are estimated, TRUE fits one pair shared by all communities (see damocles_fit()) and FALSE (the default) one pair per community.

sympatry

Probability that a present ancestor leaves both daughters present, used in the simulations (see simulate_damocles()); NULL estimates it with the rates.

regimes

Optional regime of each edge of tree, in the order of tree$edge (a factor or character vector), such as from clade_regimes() or from a configuration of rate shifts estimated by another method: the rates in vary are estimated separately for each regime.

edge_covariate

Optional positive number for each edge of tree, in the order of tree$edge, such as branch-specific rates of speciation estimated by another method: the rates in vary change with it as \(\mathrm{rate} \cdot (x / \bar{x}_g)^\beta\), where \(x\) is the covariate and \(\bar{x}_g\) its geometric mean, with rate and \(\beta\) estimated. Give regimes or edge_covariate, not both.

vary

Which rates change among regimes or with edge_covariate: "both", "gamma" or "mu"; the other one is a single rate for the whole tree.

Value

A data frame of class mc_damocles_test, one row per community, with the richness, the parameters used (gamma, mu, or the columns of the fit with regimes or edge_covariate, and sympatry; NA for rates given per edge) and their log-likelihood when estimated, and, for mpd and mntd, the observed value, the standardised effect size and p-value against the DAMOCLES null (ses_mpd_damocles, p_mpd_damocles, ...) and against random draws (ses_mpd_random, p_mpd_random, ...), plus n_valid.

Details

Allopatric speciation alone makes present species less related than random draws expect, so communities that look overdispersed against random draws may be consistent with the dynamic model (Pigot & Etienne 2015). Richness is not fixed in the communities simulated under DAMOCLES; simulated communities with fewer than two species have no MPD or MNTD and are left out of the null distribution, and n_valid counts the ones kept. Distances are the cophenetic distances of tree, which should hold every species of the regional pool.

Standardised effect sizes are \((x_{obs} - \bar{x}_{null}) / s_{null}\), as in summary_stats(): negative values mean the species present are more closely related than expected (clustering) and positive values that they are less related (overdispersion). Note that DAMOCLES::DAMOCLES_bootstrap() reports the opposite sign. The p-values are lower-tail ranks, \((r + 1) / (n + 1)\), with \(r\) the number of null values at or below the observed one and \(n\) the number of valid null values; values near one point to overdispersion.

References

Pigot, A. L., & Etienne, R. S. (2015). A new dynamic null model for phylogenetic community structure. Ecology Letters, 18, 153–163. doi:10.1111/ele.12395

See also

simulate_damocles(), damocles_fit().

Other dynamic null model: clade_regimes(), confint.mc_damocles_fit(), damocles_loglik(), damocles_lrt(), simulate_damocles()

Examples

set.seed(3)
tr <- treeshapesim::sim_tree_shape(40)
comm <- simulate_damocles(tr, gamma = 1, mu = 1, n = 2)
damocles_test(comm, tr, n_sim = 99)
#> Phylogenetic structure against the DAMOCLES null model (Pigot & Etienne 2015)
#> 99 null communities per model; SES < 0: clustering, SES > 0: overdispersion
#>      richness gamma    mu  mpd ses_mpd_damocles p_mpd_damocles ses_mpd_random
#> sim1        5  5.85 37.27 1.64          0.54759          0.810          0.730
#> sim2        7  2.03  5.65 1.54         -0.00356          0.414          0.264
#>      p_mpd_random  mntd ses_mntd_damocles p_mntd_damocles ses_mntd_random
#> sim1         0.78 0.878           -0.0181           0.550          -0.171
#> sim2         0.53 0.652           -0.7662           0.222          -0.458
#>      p_mntd_random
#> sim1          0.45
#> sim2          0.36
